title: Basic Structure of Constitution and Amendments

faqs.q: Which case first ruled that Fundamental Rights can be amended by Parliament under Article 368?
faqs.e: The Shankari Prasad case (1951) challenged the validity of the First Amendment Act, which had curtailed the right to property, prompting this first challenge to Parliament's amending power under Article 368.

faqs.q: Under Article 13, the term 'law' was held not to include which of the following?
Which case re-affirmed that a constitutional amendment act is not a law within Article 13?
faqs.e: The Sajjan Singh case was decided in 1964.

faqs.q: The Golak Nath case (1967) challenged the validity of which Amendment Act?
faqs.e: This Amendment Act (1964) had inserted certain state acts into the Ninth Schedule. In this case, the Supreme Court held that Fundamental Rights occupy a transcendental and immutable position.

faqs.q: Which Amendment Act was Parliament's response to the Golak Nath judgement?
faqs.e: The 24th Amendment Act was enacted in 1971, amending Articles 13 and 368. It also made it obligatory for the President to give assent to a constitutional amendment bill — before this Act, the President could withhold assent or return the bill for reconsideration.

faqs.q: The Kesavananda Bharati case (1973) overruled the Supreme Court's earlier judgement in which case?
faqs.e: The Kesavananda Bharati case upheld the validity of the 24th Amendment Act, and laid down the doctrine of basic structure.

faqs.q: The doctrine of basic structure was first reaffirmed in which subsequent case?
faqs.e: This case was decided in 1975. It invalidated a provision of the 39th Amendment Act, which had kept election disputes involving the Prime Minister and the Speaker of Lok Sabha outside the jurisdiction of all courts.

faqs.q: Which Amendment Act declared that no constitutional amendment can be questioned in any court?
faqs.e: The 42nd Amendment Act was enacted in 1976. It amended Article 368 to declare Parliament's constituent power unlimited.

faqs.q: The Minerva Mills case invalidated a provision of the 42nd Amendment Act for excluding which basic feature?
faqs.e: The Minerva Mills case was decided in 1980.

faqs.q: The Waman Rao case clarified that the basic structure doctrine applies to amendments enacted after which date?
faqs.e: This date corresponds to the judgement in the Kesavananda Bharati case.

faqs.q:
Consider the following statements:
(I) The Golak Nath case reversed the Supreme Court's earlier stand taken in the Shankari Prasad and Sajjan Singh cases
(II) The Golak Nath case held that a constitutional amendment act is a law within the meaning of Article 13
(III) The Golak Nath case upheld the validity of the 24th Amendment Act
Which of the above is/are correct?
faqs.e: The 24th Amendment Act was enacted after Golak Nath in reaction to it, and its validity was upheld later in the Kesavananda Bharati case.

faqs.q:
With reference to the following pairs, consider:
(I) Golak Nath case – 1967
(II) Kesavananda Bharati case – 1973
(III) Minerva Mills case – 1976
Which of the pairs given above is/are correctly matched?
faqs.e: The Minerva Mills case was decided in 1980, not 1976.

faqs.q: Powers of the Supreme Court under which Articles have been recognised as part of the basic structure?
Powers of the High Courts under which Articles have been recognised as part of the basic structure?

Consider the following statements:
(I) Federal character of the Constitution is a recognised basic feature
(II) Secular character of the Constitution is a recognised basic feature
(III) Single citizenship is a recognised basic feature
Which of the above is/are correct?
faqs.e: Single citizenship is not listed among the elements of the basic structure; federal and secular character are.

faqs.q: Which of the following is NOT an element of the basic structure?
"Harmony and balance between Fundamental Rights and Directive Principles" is an element of which doctrine?
Which case first declared "effective access to justice" as an element of the basic structure?

With reference to the following pairs, consider:
(I) L. Chandra Kumar case (1997) – Powers of the High Courts under Articles 226 and 227
(II) Ram Jethmalani case (2011) – Powers of the Supreme Court under Article 32
(III) Namit Sharma case (2012) – Judicial review
Which of the pairs given above is/are correctly matched?
faqs.e: The Namit Sharma case (2012) declared "freedom and dignity of the individual," not judicial review.

faqs.q: Which Article of the Constitution deals with the powers of Parliament to amend the Constitution?
Article 368 falls under which Part of the Constitution?
The rule that Parliament cannot amend the 'basic structure' of the Constitution was laid down in which case?
An amendment bill under Article 368 can be initiated in which of the following?

options.b: Either House of Parliament or a state legislature

faqs.q: An amendment bill under Article 368 can be introduced by whom?

options.b: Either a minister or a private member

faqs.a: Either a minister or a private member
faqs.e: Introduction of the bill does not require the prior permission of the president.

faqs.q: Passage of a constitutional amendment bill in each House requires which kind of majority?

Consider the following statements regarding the special majority required under Article 368:
(I) It means a majority of the total membership of the House
(II) It means a majority of two-thirds of members present and voting
(III) 'Total membership' excludes vacant seats from the count
Which of the above is/are correct?
faqs.e: 'Total membership' means the total number of members comprising the House irrespective of vacancies or absentees, so statement III is incorrect.

faqs.q: In case of a disagreement between the two Houses over a constitutional amendment bill, which of the following applies?

options.d: There is no provision for a joint sitting

faqs.a: There is no provision for a joint sitting

faqs.q: Ratification by state legislatures is required only when a bill seeks to amend which kind of provisions?
Ratification of a constitutional amendment bill by state legislatures requires which kind of majority?
The Constitution of India can be amended in how many ways?
Amendments made by a simple majority of Parliament outside the scope of Article 368 are treated as amendments of the Constitution for the purposes of Article 368?

options.a: False, they are not deemed amendments under Article 368
options.b: True, they are treated as such
options.c: Only if passed by both Houses separately

faqs.a: False, they are not deemed amendments under Article 368

faqs.q:
Consider the following provisions of the Constitution:
(I) Formation of new states and alteration of boundaries of existing states
(II) Quorum in Parliament
(III) Election of the President and its manner
Which of the above can be amended by a simple majority of Parliament outside Article 368?
faqs.e: Election of the President and its manner requires a special majority of Parliament along with ratification by half the states, not a simple majority.

faqs.q: Which of the following is amendable by a simple majority of Parliament outside Article 368?

options.b: Use of English language in Parliament
options.c: Distribution of legislative powers between Union and states

faqs.a: Use of English language in Parliament

faqs.q: The Fifth Schedule, dealing with administration of scheduled areas and scheduled tribes, can be amended by which kind of majority?

options.b: Special majority with ratification by states

faqs.q: Fundamental Rights and Directive Principles of State Policy can be amended by which kind of majority?

options.d: Special majority with ratification by states

faqs.q:
Consider the following provisions:
(I) Distribution of legislative powers between the Union and the states
(II) Representation of states in Parliament
(III) Article 368 itself
Which of the above require a special majority of Parliament along with ratification by half of the state legislatures?
The provision relating to the Goods and Services Tax Council was added to the list of federal provisions requiring state ratification by which Amendment Act?
faqs.e: The 101st Amendment Act (2016) relates to Article 279-A, which deals with the Goods and Services Tax Council.

faqs.q: If a bill amending federal provisions is ratified by half of the states, what happens if the remaining states take no action?

options.c: A fresh bill must be introduced

faqs.e: There is also no time limit within which states must give their consent.

faqs.q: Unlike in the USA, Indian state legislatures generally cannot initiate a constitutional amendment bill, except for passing a resolution requesting which of the following?

options.a: Creation or abolition of legislative councils

faqs.a: Creation or abolition of legislative councils

faqs.q: As per critics of the amendment procedure, ratification of federal provisions in India requires the consent of how many states, compared to three-fourths in the USA?
Which of the following is a criticism of the Indian Constitution's amendment procedure?

options.a: There is no provision for a joint sitting in case of a deadlock over an amendment bill
options.b: The President can reject any amendment bill
options.c: A joint sitting is compulsory for every amendment bill
options.d: State legislatures can independently amend federal provisions

faqs.a: There is no provision for a joint sitting in case of a deadlock over an amendment bill
faqs.e: A provision for a joint sitting does exist for ordinary bills, unlike constitutional amendment bills.

faqs.q: Which political scientist observed that the Indian Constitution's amending process 'strikes a good balance between flexibility and rigidity'?
